chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umayr, from Sa'id al-Azraq, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding
a man who killed a believing man. He said: 'It will be said to him: Die whichever death you like — if you like, as a Jew; if you like, as a Christian; if you like, as a Magian.'

key_terms.مُؤْمِناً: A believer — one who holds correct faith; in Shia tradition this implies a Shia Muslim
key_terms.مِيتَةٍ: Manner of death/dying; refers here to the spiritual state in which one dies
key_terms.يَهُودِيًّا / نَصْرَانِيًّا / مَجُوسِيًّ: Jew / Christian / Magian — religions outside of Islam, symbolizing dying in a state of disbelief

ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for killing a believer according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) pronounces an eschatological ruling on one who kills a believer: in the next life, such a person will be given the grim 'choice' of dying in a state of disbelief — as a Jew, Christian, or Magian. This is not a literal choice but a declaration of spiritual ruin, indicating that the murderer has effectively abandoned true faith. The gravity of this ruling reflects the sanctity of the believer's life in Shia Islamic jurisprudence and theology.
